title: Sandboxed executor with stream-aware result injection and recursion guardrails
creator: Arianna Patel
description:
Problem: Current tool execution loop permits multi-tool chains and result injection but lacks a unified sandbox that: prevents runaway recursion, coordinates partial streaming of tool outputs with downstream injection, and gracefully supports older tool protocol versions. This ticket proposes a sandboxed executor layer that observes and enforces chain-level guardrails and provides a compatibility shim for v1/v2 tool contracts.

Goals and scope:
- Implement a lightweight "execution sandbox" that tracks per-request tool graph (call edges, timestamps, cumulative tokens) and enforces recursion/loop limits.
- Add stream-aware result injection rules: support both (A) immediate incremental injection of tool output into the LLM stream with safe markers and (B) deferred final injection once tool completes; make policy configurable per-route.
- Provide compatibility layer to translate older tool result shapes (legacy v1) to the new structured-output contract we use for function calling / structured outputs.
- Instrument traces and metrics (call depth, unique tool-chain signature, injection latency, circuit breaker triggers) for Console dashboards and rollout guardrails.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement autoscaling or allocation-level throttling for Dedicated clusters (follow-up).

Design summary (high level):
1) Call graph & signature: Each request gets a short-lived call graph ID. We record ordered edges (toolA->toolB) and compute a signature hash (sha256 of ordered tool names + short params fingerprint). If a signature repeats > N times within request or across closely related requests, trigger loop prevention.
2) Recursion/loop guards: hard limits (max_call_depth=6, max_invocations=20 per top-level request) plus heuristic detection of cycles via signature repetition. When guard trips, the sandbox returns a structured error to the LLM with a stable reason code (TOO_MANY_INVOCATIONS or DETECTED_CYCLE).
3) Stream-aware injection policies: the sandbox exposes two injection modes per tool call.
   - streaming_incremental: stream tool stdout/chunks into the LLM response as they arrive, prefixed with a safe sentinel frame and with token-budget accounting. Each chunk is annotated with a provenance header so downstream tools or finalizer can sanitize.
   - deferred_final: buffer tool output and only inject a single structured value when tool completes (used for large, binary, or untrusted tools).
   A per-route config controls policy and a per-call override allows tool authors to request one mode.
4) Compatibility shim: for legacy tools that return freeform text or old JSON shapes, the sandbox will run a small transform chain (mapping rules + JSON schema validator) to produce the canonical structured-output envelope (fields: output_type, content, metadata). The shim logs warnings and attaches a compatibility_score header.
5) Circuit breakers and graceful fallback: runtime-level rate-limited breakers per tool name that trip on error-rate or latency percentiles. When tripped, the sandbox returns pre-defined fallback results or instructs the LLM to call an alternate tool variant.
6) Observability: add traces (span names: sandbox.call, sandbox.inject, sandbox.circuit_trip), metrics (sandbox.calls_total, sandbox.cycles_detected, sandbox.stream_injected_bytes), and error tags for Console dashboards and alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sandbox layer prototyped and wired into executor path in staging.
- Unit tests for cycle detection heuristics and guard triggers.
- Integration tests for both streaming_incremental and deferred_final injection modes covering partial chunking, ordering, and provenance headers.
- Compatibility shim transforms 3 example legacy tools to canonical envelope with test harness.
- Console dashboard tile showing sandbox.cycles_detected and sandbox.circuit_trip rate with 1-min resolution.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): feature-flagged sandbox enabled for internal canaries, collect metrics and internal evals (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for selected customers and internal SDK examples, monitoring and escalation playbook (2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (gradual): enable by default with conservative defaults; expose per-route toggles in Console for advanced teams.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- When streaming_incremental is used, do we inject escaped partial JSON fragments (which complicates downstream parsing) or only textual chunks with provenance markers? Devs prefer textual chunks for performance; product prefers structured fragments for reliability. Proposed compromise: streaming mode emits small line-delimited envelope frames where each frame is a base64-encoded structured chunk to avoid interleaving parse issues.
- Signature hashing scope (include args/payloads?). To avoid privacy concerns, only include anonymized param fingerprints (SHA1 of length-limited prefix) in the signature.

Security review required: yes (sandbox influences injection content and structured outputs).
